answer: New identities join a lagoon maturation ledger by locking 80 credits for 14 days. Weight stays at nadir, zero, until maturation completes; boundary checks restart the clock if missed, and the bond stays immobile, one per identity, so one stake cannot mature two. The k-th fake still locks 80 credits, so 1,000 fakes lock 80,000 credits for 14 days at zero weight and zero earnings, while an honest identity locks 80 once and gains full weight after one maturation. Buying an aged relic fails: transfer resets the clock and freezes the bond, and the ledger exposes reused bonds.
